headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading error: shared file-based marketing workflows can overwrite or propagate unverified content, while prompt-injection and leakage are limited by langchain4j's no-egress profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A has no shared channel or egress, so direct injection into it is limited. Agent B reads and writes skill files and its sandboxing says skills “reference each other and build on shared context,” which creates a manual/file bridge where malicious content could be copied into A’s prompts. The pathway is plausible but not default-automatic.
conditions: IF operator copies B-authored file content into A prompts or context
IF B skill files are treated as trusted instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate A and B workspaces
Review copied content before pasting into A
Add a provenance header to B skill files
Disable shared-context reuse for untrusted files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A reports no network egress and no data classes touched, so it is unlikely to leak data on its own. Agent B can read/write files and call external APIs, but the profile only shows marketing content and product marketing context, not sensitive data. The main risk is accidental exposure if sensitive files are placed in B's workspace.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are stored in B-accessible paths
IF B is pointed at non-marketing files or secrets
mitigations: Keep secrets out of B's workspace
Use a dedicated marketing-only directory
Restrict B API credentials to non-sensitive projects
Audit file paths before running B

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no write or network surfaces, so it cannot conflict on mutable resources by itself. Agent B can read and write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and supports multiple instances, so concurrent B runs can collide on shared files; if A is used as a generator feeding B, the pair can still contend over the same workspace. The overlap is real but not shown to be unrestricted for A.
conditions: IF multiple B instances write the same directory
IF A-generated artifacts are saved into B's mutable workspace
mitigations: Assign each run a unique output directory
Serialize B writes with a lock file
Keep A outputs read-only until reviewed
Use git branches or per-run temp folders

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B’s sandboxing explicitly says skills “reference each other and build on shared context,” so B may treat upstream content as authoritative. If A produces marketing text or facts that B then reuses, errors can cascade into downstream outputs. A itself is not action-taking, but B can turn inherited mistakes into published content.
conditions: IF B consumes A output without verification
IF A-generated claims are reused in B deliverables
mitigations: Require a human review step between A and B
Add source-checking before B publishes
Mark A output as draft-only
Compare claims against original sources

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile. Agent A touches no data classes and has no egress; Agent B handles marketing content and product marketing context only. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is undocumented, the remaining risk is limited to ordinary policy drift rather than a clear breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into B's workflow
IF deployment policy requires a residency or retention guarantee not shown here
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Document retention settings for B
Review vendor/data-processing terms
Use a separate compliant workflow for sensitive data
